event.name: UFC 330
event.notes: Discovery pulls recent uploads from each capper channel and keeps the ones whose title matches settings.discovery.title_contains. Add entries to "videos" only to pin a specific video by hand.

comments.comment: Says he isn't super confident but Abdul-Malik is younger, more physical, with height, reach and power advantages over a hittable Stoltzfus.

Both cappers pick Mansur: Angelo cites a giant grappling gap plus powerful hands and desperation after his TKO loss, while Jacob thinks the striking edge is the difference since Stoltzfus is stationary and hittable.
Athletic freak with reach and better wrestling against a middle-of-the-road middleweight; expects him to take Stoltzfus down and smash him early despite the high price.
Picks Abdul-Malik to defeat Stoltzfus.
Dern is better everywhere - striking, grappling, even wrestling - and is all-time tough; Robertson has no path without takedowns, and capper says he can't see how she wins.
Robertson's takedowns are still weak and she gave up reversals to Lemos; Dern is far higher-level on the ground and he prefers her striking and chin too.
Picks Dern in the co-main event.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhache

comments.comment: Angelo says the wrestling is simply too good and Makhachev should take Garry down, though he respects Garry and won't bet it; Jacob agrees Garry's hands won't keep Islam out.
One of his most confident favorites on the card: Makhachev has passed every test, is durable without the weight cut, and Garry's year with Oliveira won't be enough.
Picks Makhachev in the main event.
Calls it the easiest pick on the card: Orolbai is far better on the ground, has wins over ranked opposition, and Wells will get taken down and submitted or rocked into a panic takedown into a d'arce.
Wells won't handle Orolbai's grappling as the fight wears on; Orolbai has the edge in both striking volume/technique and wrestling, so he should reach a dominant position and find the sub.

picks.selection: Mansur Abdul-Malik by KO/TKO in round 1 or 2

comments.comment: Abdul-Malik is better technically on the feet, far more powerful and explosive, and his takedown defense removes Stoltzfus's best weapon; very confident.
Abdul-Malik's power and brutal ground and pound against Stoltzfus' bad chin, poor striking defense and poor takedown defense should equal a knockout.
Barboza is 40, slower and less durable after a bad knockout loss; Ribovics is clean, durable and busy, has never really lost to a striker and should stay a step ahead.
Stated as his main card pick to defeat Barboza.

Orolbai is better than Wells at everything Wells does best, should take him down instantly and maul him on top; capper thinks he should be a much larger favorite and calls him the overwhelmingly confident pick to open the card.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhache
picks.selection: Islam Makhachev by submission in round 4

comments.comment: Makhachev has solved every advantage Garry has before (size, reach, boxing), is elite in scrambles with the d'arce and back takes, and Garry can't finish him or out-decision him with Khabib game-planning.
Nobody defends Makhachev's takedowns and Garry lacks one-punch power, so Garry would have to win a decision; Makhachev drags him late for a finish.
Despite giving Garry a 35-40% chance and outlining a game plan for him, he still picks Islam by submission, believing Islam should be able to secure takedowns and control time.

picks.selection: Jose Ochoa by KO/TKO in round 2

comments.comment: Vowed never to pick Johnson again; Johnson is hittable to the left hook and starts slow, while Ochoa has crisp boxing and in his view beat Alibayev.
Ochoa's rare power at 125 will get Johnson's respect, Johnson is coming off a bad KO loss and fighting too often, and he won't offensively wrestle Ochoa.
Expects the win most likely by KO.
On a three-fight win streak at 170 with wrestling pace and pressure, while Wells is nearly 40 and had been on a losing skid; he can take damage and keep coming.
Angelo thinks Fernandes can wrestle his way to a win and repeat his flow-state performance vs Gam, though he calls it a very close fight.
Doesn't fully trust Turner's comeback after his early retirement, and Fernandes is solid, well-rounded and mixes in takedowns well; likely decision or late TKO, but a lower confidence pick.
Angelo says Oralby is a different level of wrestler and will dominate a 40-year-old Wells whenever he wants; the odds are understated but too expensive to bet heavily.

picks.selection: Ramiz Brahimaj by submission in round 1

comments.comment: Official prediction is Brahimaj via submission in round one or two given Magny's history of early submission losses.
Even-odds fight but he favors Brahimaj's explosiveness and quick finishing ability, and Magny has repeatedly gotten into bad grappling spots and been submitted recently.
Brahimaj only wins by submission and usually in round one, and Magny has always struggled with submission defense; the fight is either a Brahimaj finish or a Magny decision.
12 of Brahimaj's 13 wins are by submission and Magny has been submitted repeatedly; capper says he'll watch for the prop when it drops and take a shot at it.
Predicts Luque shoots a bad takedown and Gore lands another standing guillotine, having already got three in the UFC.

picks.fight: Ian Machado Garry vs Islam Makhache
picks.selection: Fight does not go the distance

comments.comment: Jacob wanted Islam inside the distance at +150 but took fight doesn't go the distance at +120 to also cover a weird Garry finish; he expects Islam to wear Garry down and submit him.
Alvarez's fatal flaw is takedown defense and Njokuani never wrestles, so Alvarez gets the long-range striking match he wants against a hesitant opponent.
Expects the wrestling and grappling output to lead to a submission finish in round two or three.
Fernando is a massive LFA double champion with power and better level of competition, and Tobias struggles on the feet and plods around, so he expects a first-round knockout.
Calls Fernando a special talent with huge reach, fast varied striking; expects him to stop the takedowns and knock Tobias out early.
Thinks the fight should be even odds and Tobias is value, but ultimately Fernando is the more complete, technical and versatile striker; explicitly a low confidence pick.

picks.selection: Ramiz Brahimaj in round 1 or round 2

comments.comment: Jacob says he will definitely have action on Brahimaj early — first or second round submission — since Brahimaj chases the guillotine relentlessly and Magny is lazy with his head position.
Urbay is the better wrestler (19 takedowns vs Chris Curtis) and Wells isn't enough of a submission threat; Urbay has been finding second-round submissions.
Jacob finds +300 interesting because Wells puts himself in bad grappling positions and Oralby can snatch a submission when Wells tries to scramble.
Won't back a 5'8" fighter at 185; Johnson has been trapped in wrestling positions before, so he expects Nolan to extend the fight and outgrapple him.
Both like Fernando's striking, length and athleticism over Tobias's brute-force grappling, but at -300 in a UFC debut they are picking him without betting the moneyline.
Angelo says Luque is better everywhere and the line movement making him a dog makes no sense, but he is only picking him, not betting him.

picks.selection: Jalin Turner by first round finish

comments.comment: Suggested as a hedge alongside the Fernandes moneyline since Turner is the bigger, more dangerous finisher.
Johnson tends to give away the first round which is fatal in a 15-minute fight, and Ochoa's pressure, volume, power and speed should carry it; capper doesn't love the -335 price.
Ochoa is the younger, active, intense striker with decent takedown defense; sees it as a passing of the torch over the 36-year-old Johnson.
Picks Ochoa to beat Johnson in the featured fight.
Barboza is 40 and has absorbed massive damage recently; Ribovics is durable, high-volume and pressuring, so he expects a punches-in-bunches breakdown finish.
Ribovics' pressure, volume and power should overwhelm a 40-year-old Barboza who has taken a lot of damage; no specific round given since it could come in any of the three.
Expects the win to come most likely by KO.
Doesn't like Luque's move up to 185 at age 35 after recent poor showings, while Gore is the bigger man and dangerous with front chokes.
Low confidence play; believes Luque is battle-worn, doesn't wear damage well and has no wins at middleweight, while Gore is the stronger, more willing man.

picks.selection: Joel Alvarez by submission or ground-and-pound TKO

comments.comment: Alvarez has a ~95% finish rate and is dangerous everywhere; Njokuani can't grapple and got hit repeatedly by lesser strikers like Carlos Leal.
Njokuani has a poor record against grapplers and Alvarez has a huge grappling advantage; if he uses the wrestling he could finish early in round one or two.

picks.selection: Jalin Turner by KO/TKO in round 1

comments.comment: Medium confidence: Turner is a gifted, huge, hard-hitting lightweight and Fernandes' opposition wouldn't beat him; a naked leg kick could get him cracked early.
Turner is the side whenever he faces a non-wrestler, he's enormous for 155, his fights rarely leave round one, and the odds are close.
Thinks Brahimaj is overrated with wins only over cans, while Magny has huge height/reach, experience and a grappling edge and can pick him apart off the back foot for a decision.
Jacob takes the dog Magny as the safer pick, saying it's a tailor-made Magny fight where he weathers the early submission threat and wears Brahimaj down for the decision.
Johnson's explosiveness, power and speed should matter in the striking exchanges and get an early finish, but McConico is the more technical guy and very live as a dog; low to mid confidence.
Johnson's boxing is his real skill set and McConico hates being backed up and hit; the worry is Johnson's terrible fight IQ leading him to wrestle again.

A 50/50 fight where he takes the underdog: Luque is arguably better everywhere technically and if he hurts his opponent he'll likely club-and-sub with a front choke, though he's worried about Luque's durability.

Bad stylistic matchup for Robertson: Dern is dangerous on the ground and clearly more technical and dangerous on the feet, so if Robertson can't dominate with wrestling she loses; borderline confident-picks-list addition possibly in a two-legger.
Dern's improved striking wins the exchanges while the grappling cancels out; as an experienced champ ahead on the cards she won't risk chasing a finish.
Neither man has a clean UFC win, but based on potential, regional wins and power Johnson is the better fighter right now and should have the performance people have been expecting; odds are fine.
